objectives: Improve system reliability and avoid thermal overloads of 69 kV transmission lines which occur in scenarios were Valley Center energy storage is dispatched either in charging or discharging mode.
driver_detail: Thermal overloads (P0, P1, P3, P6) on multiple 69 kV lines caused specifically by the charging and discharging of the Valley Center energy storage (BESS). The project also retires the existing Valley Center RAS which was violating ISO S-RAS2 standard by operating in P0 conditions. The overloads are directly caused by battery storage dispatch operations—a renewable/storage resource integration issue—not by load growth or equipment aging.
alternatives_rejected: Status Quo Not recommended since thermal overloads occur in P0 conditions which trigger existing Valley Center RAS, contradicting ISO S-RAS2 standard. May 23, 2024
interim_solution: Rely on operational actions along with the use of the existing Valley Center RAS to restrict the charging and discharing of Valley Center energy storage.

project_name: Mira Loma 500 kV Bus Additional SCD Mitigation
brief_description: Replace additional two (2) 40 KA circuit breakers at Mira Loma 500 kV with new 63 kA rated CBs
objectives: Address the short circuit duty (SCD) concerns on additional two 500 kV circuit breakers at Mira Loma 500/230 kV substation that are loaded to greater than 95% and even 100% of the rated 40 KA SCD capability in the near term and the long term due to system changes
driver_detail: Two additional 40 kA circuit breakers at Mira Loma 500/230 kV substation are loaded to >95% (near-term) and approaching 100% (long-term) of their rated SCD capability 'due to system changes.' This is an extension of the 2022-2023 TPP Mira Loma 500 kV SCD project (which already approved replacement of four CBs), where the same system changes—driven by new renewable generation interconnection in the SCE 500 kV network—are stressing the remaining breakers. Equip_aging: existing 40 kA breakers are underrated for current fault levels. Renewable: system changes driving elevated SCD are consistent with renewable portfolio additions at Mira Loma 500 kV.
alternatives_rejected: Status Quo Not recommended due to potential reliability and safety concern for new generation interconnection May 23, 2024
interim_solution: Limited operation of generation in the area as complex operating procedures to manage overstressed CBs

brief_description: Install a 25 MVar shunt reactor at Inyo 230 kV substation (SCE side)
objectives: Mitigate real time high voltage issues at Inyo 230 kV bus. The actual bus voltages are far beyond the voltage limits in the CAISO planning standard. Mitigate the NERC Category P5 high voltage identified in plannind study starting in 2025.
driver_detail: Real-time high voltage at Inyo 230 kV bus exceeding limits, plus NERC Category P5 high voltage violations identified in planning study starting 2025. Project installs a 25 MVAR shunt reactor at Inyo 230 kV substation (SCE side). Supersedes the previously approved Control 115 kV Shunt Reactor Project. The Inyo area is in the desert with long lightly-loaded 230 kV lines prone to Ferranti-effect high voltage. No load growth or equipment aging factor.
alternatives_rejected: The project was approved in 2022-2023 TPP. However, upon further evaluation, installing shunt reactor at SCE side Inyo 230 kV bus was more effective in addressing the high voltage issue and was a more viable location for construction. The Inyo 230 kV shunt reactor project will supersede the Control 115 kV shunt reactor project. May 23, 2024
interim_solution: Utilize the system operating bulletins SOB80 and SOB17

project_name: Etiwanda 230 kV Bus SCD Mitigation Project
brief_description: Replace twelve (12) 230 kV circuit breakers at Etiwanda currently rated 63 kA tested at X/R ratio of 17 with new 63 kA rated circuit breakers tested at X/R ratio of 35
objectives: Short-circuit duty (SCD) studies indicate that the twelve 230 kV circuit breakers are expected to be loaded to greater than 95% of their rated three-phase SCD capability in the near term (2025) and to 100% in the long term (2035).
driver_detail: Twelve 230 kV circuit breakers at Etiwanda substation are projected to be loaded to >95% of rated SCD in near-term (2025) and 100% in long-term (2035). Existing breakers are rated 63 kA but tested at X/R ratio of 17, insufficient for asymmetric fault currents at the current and projected SCD levels; replaced with 63 kA breakers tested at X/R ratio of 35. Equip_aging: existing breakers cannot handle the system's elevated asymmetric fault currents. Renewable: the increasing X/R ratio at Etiwanda is characteristic of SCE's growing renewable generation portfolio interconnecting to this key 230 kV substation, consistent with other SCE SCD projects in this cycle.
alternatives_rejected: Develop operating procedure to open 230 kV transmission lines in real-time May 23, 2024

brief_description: Install a 10 MVAR Shunt Capacitor at Covelo 60 kV
objectives: P1 low voltages starting 2025 at Covelo 60 kV substation
driver_detail: Category P1 low voltage violations starting in 2025 at Covelo 60 kV substation. Covelo is at the end of a long radial 60 kV line in Mendocino County. Installing a 10 MVAR shunt capacitor addresses the post-contingency voltage deficit. Need date 2025 indicates an existing structural voltage deficiency on this radial line, not a load-growth or equipment-aging issue.
alternatives_rejected: Installing SVC is not recommended because of higher cost May 23, 2024

brief_description: Reconductor 7.2 miles on the Martin-Sneath Lane 60 kV line and 2.5 miles on the Millbrae-Sneath Lane 60 kV line
objectives: Mitigate the thermal violations in the Martin-Millbrae 60 kV system under P1 contingencies. Increase the load serving capability and customer reliability in the area.
driver_detail: P1 contingency overloads on Martin-Sneath Lane and Millbrae-Sneath Lane 60 kV lines driven by explicit high load growth. Report states: 'The load forecast indicates high load growth in this area due to multiple business load requests resulting in PG&E planning to expand the load serving capacity.' Project reconductors two 60 kV line sections (7.2 and 2.5 miles) with larger conductor to achieve at least 1100–1200 Amps, indicating the existing conductors are the physical bottleneck (equip_aging). Load growth is the explicit cause.
load_growth_evidence: Report states: 'The load forecast indicates high load growth in this area due to multiple business load requests.' PG&E plans to expand load serving capacity at Sneath Lane substation due to increased demand.
alternatives_rejected: Energy storage. This alternative is not recommended because the energy storage charging capability is limited by the existing transmission capacity and will be further limited by the expected load increase. May 23, 2024
interim_solution: Millbrae Reverse Power Relay and Open Sneath Lane 60 kV ring bus by opening CBs 6032 & 6052 during winter peak hours. Load transfer to the Halfmoon Bay area.

brief_description: Install a 200 MVA 3-phase 230/60 kV transformer with LTC at Atlantic substation
objectives: To resolve the NERC category P0 high voltage violations at Atlantic 60 kV Substation starting in 2028 and improve operational reliability.
driver_detail: P0 base-case high voltage violations at Atlantic 60 kV Substation starting in 2028. Installs a 200 MVA 3-phase 230/60 kV transformer with LTC to regulate the 60 kV bus voltage. The project need date of 2028 and P0 category indicate an existing voltage management gap independent of load growth or generation retirement. Re-scope of an earlier Atlantic High Voltage Mitigation project.
alternatives_rejected: • Not recommended due to not mitigating P0 high voltage violations Alternative 2: Install regulator and spare single-phase bank • Not recommended due to missing wider score i.e. improved customer reliability, operational flexibility and providing a back-up source May 23, 2024

brief_description: Reconductor Camden-Kingsburg 70 kV and add voltage support
objectives: To reduce base case overloads on Camden-Kingsburg 70 kV line
driver_detail: P0 (base-case) thermal overloads on Camden-Kingsburg 70 kV line driven explicitly by local load growth. Report states operations has observed 'over 90% loading on Camden-Kingsburg 70 kV line during peak conditions due to the local load growth' and 'as a result of the increased demand, low voltages were observed at Camden substation in all near-term and long-term summer peak scenarios.' Reconductoring to 800 Amps addresses the conductor capacity gap (equip_aging). A 30 MVAR capacitor addresses concurrent low voltage issues (voltage). Load growth is the stated primary cause.
load_growth_evidence: Report states: 'Operations has observed over 90% loading on Camden-Kingsburg 70 kV line during peak conditions due to the local load growth.' PG&E distribution load forecast indicates additional loads will be transferred to Camden substation, resulting in P0 overloads and low voltages in all near-term and long-term scenarios.
alternatives_rejected: Energy storage and voltage support is not recommended due to space limitation and battery will be a new P1 limitation that needs mitigation May 23, 2024

brief_description: Add additional 230/70 kV bank at Gates
objectives: To reduce overloads on 70 kV and 115 kV lines due to loss of Gates 230/70 kV bank 5
driver_detail: Category P1 and P3 contingency overloads on multiple 70 kV and 115 kV lines when the main Gates 230/70 kV transformer bank #5 is lost. The existing backup supply (Schindler 115/70 kV bank #1 and Coalinga #1–San Miguel 70 kV line) is insufficient to serve the load without overloads. Adding a second 230/70 kV transformer at Gates provides redundant capacity and eliminates the single-transformer-loss vulnerability. Need date 2025 confirms an existing infrastructure deficiency. No explicit load growth stated.
interim_solution: Operating solution Project Cost Alternatives Considered but Rejected California ISO/I&OP $36M - $72M • • Energy storatge is not recommended as around 100MW is needed to mitigate all overloads and there isn’t sufficient capacity to charge this size of battery Converting entire 70 kV to 115 kV is not cost-effective H-13 May 23, 2024

brief_description: Add a double circuit between Reedley-Dinuba 70 kV line #2 and upgrade rating of existing Reedley-Dinuba 70 kV line #1 and upgrade Reedley 230/70 kV bank
objectives: Mitigate 70 kV line overloads and bank #4 overloads caused by certain P1 contingencies
driver_detail: Category P1 contingency overloads on Reedley-Dinuba #1 and Reedley-Orosi 70 kV lines in both near-term and long-term scenarios; transformer bank #4 overload under loss of bank #2 in long-term. Previously approved energy storage at Dinuba (12 MW) does not mitigate constraints. Project reconductors existing 70 kV lines, adds a double-circuit Reedley-Dinuba #2 line, and upgrades the transformer bank rating. No explicit load growth or renewable driver.
interim_solution: Operating solution Project Cost Alternatives Considered but Rejected California ISO/I&OP TBD Reconductoring the 70 kV lines, upgrade bank with existing Dinuba BESS. This alternative still doesn’t fully mitigate all overloads for 2035 and beyond. H-14 May 23, 2024

project_name: Diablo Canyon Area 230 kV High Voltage Mitigation Project
brief_description: Add 120 Mvar shunt reactor (3X40 MVAR or 4X30 MVAR) and removal of one or two shunt capacitor steps at Mesa 115 kV
objectives: Mitigate high-voltages observed in real time around or right after midnight, during low demand and zero solar output periods at Diablo Canyon 230 kV substation
driver_detail: Real-time high voltages above 242 kV (limit) observed at Diablo Canyon 230 kV substation around midnight when area load is low, local solar output is zero, and bulk transfer is low. The high voltage is caused by the charging capacitance of 230 kV lines combined with low load and zero solar conditions—a structural voltage management issue at this substation, not load growth or equipment aging. Project installs 120 MVAR shunt reactors at Mesa 115 kV bus to regulate the 230 kV voltage.
alternatives_rejected: Alternatives include STATCOM installations at Mesa 115 kV or 230 kV, or Morro Bay 230 kV, or Diablo 230 kV but were rejected due to large costs associated with the upgrades. May 23, 2024

project_name: Crazy Horse Canyon-Salinas-Soledad #1 and #2 115 kV Line Reconductoring
brief_description: Re-conductor sections of CHCSS-Salinas-Soledad #1 and #2 115 kV lines
objectives: Reduce overloads on CHCSS-Natividad and Natividad-Salinas sections for a Mosslanding-Salinas #1 115 kV line

The text notes overloads 'as a result of the increased demand' during peak loading but does not provide explicit load growth projections or figures. Reconductoring to at least 1200 Amps summer emergency rating addresses the existing conductor capacity deficiency on these Central Coast 115 kV lines. Need date 2025 confirms a near-term capacity gap.
alternatives_rejected: Loop Mosslanding-Del Monte #1 and #2 double circuit into Salinas substation not possible due to space constraint at Salinas May 23, 2024

brief_description: Reconductor Vaca-Plainfield 60 kV (about 30 miles) to achieve minimum conductor rating of 635 AMPS for summer normal and 741 AMPS for summer emergency rating
objectives: Addressing the near-term overloads on the Vaca-Plainfield 60 kV line resulting from NERC Category P0 and P1 contingencies.
driver_detail: P0 (base-case) overload on Vaca-Plainfield 60 kV line in the near term. The Plainfield substation is radially served and the existing 60 kV line lacks sufficient capacity under normal operating conditions. Reconductoring approximately 30 miles to achieve 635 Amps normal / 741 Amps summer emergency rating addresses the physical conductor capacity gap. Need date 2025 confirms existing deficiency. No load growth or renewable driver stated.

brief_description: Reconductoring Rio Oso – W. Sacramento 115 kV line as original re-rate of this line as a part of Vaca Dixon reinforcement project approved in 2017-18 TPP is no longer viable due to aging infrastructure.
objectives: Addressing overloads and voltage criteria violations within the 115 kV and 60 kV transmission system connecting Vaca Dixon, Davis, Rio Oso, and Brighton substations under NERC Category P0 - P7 contingencies.
driver_detail: Two explicit drivers: (1) Equip_aging: 'due to aging infrastructure, the re-rate of the Rio Oso-West Sacramento 115 kV line (as a part of Vaca-Dixon Reinforcement project approved in 2017-18 TPP) is no longer viable.' The aging conductor cannot safely operate at the higher rating needed. (2) Load_growth: 'substantial distribution load interconnections have been requested in this area.' P0–P7 thermal and voltage violations identified. Reconductoring ~26 miles of the 115 kV line addresses both the aging conductor limitation and the new load demand.
load_growth_evidence: Report states 'substantial distribution load interconnections have been requested in this area,' contributing to the need for higher capacity beyond what re-rating could provide.
interim_solution: Operational Solution Project Cost Alternatives Considered but Rejected California ISO/I&OP $48.7M - $97.4M N/A H-18 May 23, 2024

brief_description: Reconductoring Cortina-Arbuckle 60 kV and Arbuckle-Dunnigan 60 kV sections on Cortina #1 60 kV line
objectives: Addressing overloads and low voltage criteria violations within the 60 kV transmission system connecting Dunnigan, Arbuckle and Cortina substations under NERC Category P0 contingencies.
driver_detail: New load interconnection requests (EV charging station, agricultural pump, near-term 10 MW industrial load) at Dunnigan substation are causing P0 overloads (up to 140% of summer normal rating) on Cortina #1 60 kV line sections and low voltage (as low as 0.87 p.u. at Dunnigan). Load_growth: PG&E conducted a 'load interconnection system impact study for this load increase.' Equip_aging: existing conductor is undersized for even normal distribution load growth (P0 overload at 113% by 2035 under normal growth alone). Voltage: low voltage at multiple buses along the line.
load_growth_evidence: PG&E received a near-term 10 MW load interconnection request at Dunnigan substation; 0.7 MW already online in 2023, 4.2 MW in queue for 2024, plus 0.5 MW agricultural pump and 0.4 MW EV charging station applications. Even under only normal distribution load growth, P0 thermal overload at 113% appears by 2035.
interim_solution: Operating solutions Project Cost Alternatives Considered but Rejected California ISO/I&OP $47.1M - $94.3M N/A H-19 May 23, 2024

brief_description: Build new 115 kV station near Chaular; convert existing Salinas-Spence 60 kV network to 115 kV and operate Salinas-Chaular system at 115 kV
objectives: Address reliability driven concerns, including thermal overloads observed on Salinas-Firestone #1 and #2 lines 60 kV and voltage concerns near Spence 60 kV, Firestone 60 kV, and Gonzales 60 kV substations.
driver_detail: Explicit load growth: PG&E Distribution Planning has received 'a large number of load interconnection applications near Spence.' Load at Spence substation is forecast at 23.3 MW (2023), 50.8 MW (2025), and 84.6 MW (2035), far exceeding the 60 MVA substation capacity. Category P0, P1, P2, and P7 thermal overloads on Salinas-Firestone 60 kV lines (equip_aging: existing conductor infrastructure undersized for current+projected load). Low voltage concerns at Spence, Firestone, and Gonzales 60 kV substations (voltage). The previously approved Salinas-Firestone reconductor project is now insufficient due to load growth.
load_growth_evidence: PG&E Distribution Planning received 'a large number of load interconnection applications near Spence.' Load at Spence substation forecast: 23.3 MW in 2023, 50.8 MW in 2025, 84.6 MW in 2035. Report states: 'Due to load growth in the area, the previously approved Salinas-Firestone #1 and #2 reconductor project... is insufficient to address these overloads.'
alternatives_rejected: 60 kV reconductoring alternative rejected due to large conductor size required, space limitations for voltage support at Gonzales and third transformer bank at Salinas and limited increase in load serving capapcity post upgrades, 115 kV loopin and 230 kV loop-in alternatives were both rejected mainly due to imminent need for a new distribution station at 60 kV and large costs associated with the upgrades. May 23, 2024

brief_description: Reconductor of the Wheeler Ridge – Tejon 70kV line, Wheeler Ridge – San Bernard 70kV line, and San Bernard – Tejon 70kV line and replace the limiting disconnect switches
objectives: Mitigate thermal overloads on the Wheeler Ridge – Tejon 70kV line, Wheeler Ridge – San Bernard 70kV line, San Bernard – Tejon 70kV line caused by P3 overloads and additional loading at Tejon substation
driver_detail: Explicit projected load growth: 'an additional 50 MW load at San Bernard substation and 45.5 MW load at Tejon 70kV substation.' These new loads cause P3 contingency overloads on Wheeler Ridge–Tejon, Wheeler Ridge–San Bernard, and San Bernard–Tejon 70 kV lines in all near-term and long-term summer peak scenarios. Reconductoring all three lines (equip_aging) and replacing limiting disconnect switches adds 104 MW of load-serving capacity to the Tejon area.
load_growth_evidence: Report explicitly states: 'The projected local load growth, including an additional 50 MW load at San Bernard substation and 45.5 MW load at Tejon 70kV substation... results in thermal overloads.' All near-term and long-term scenarios show P3 overloads driven by these additional loads.
alternatives_rejected: Option 2: Build a new 115kV source from Wheeler Ridge to Tejon Option 2 provides less (for the radial portion) or equal (for the network addition) load serving capacity to the Tejon area than option 3, still requires some 70kV work, and is more expensive than chosen alternative. Option 3: Build a new 230kV source from Wheeler Ridge to Tejon This option is not recommended for this TPP cycle due to cost and the fact that the current recommended scope is sufficient to address the Tejon area overloads observed in this cycle. However, it may be considered in the future based on load growth projections in the Tejon pocket. May 23, 2024

brief_description: Loop French Camp substation into Bellota-Tesla #2 230 kV line to add a new 230 kV bus at French Camp. The total length of transmission circuit is about 4.4 miles.
objectives: Addressing overloads at Weber 60 kV line #2 (Weber - French Camp) starting in the near-term under NERC Category P1 contingencies.
driver_detail: P1 contingency overloads on Weber 60 kV line #2 (Weber–French Camp) starting in the near term; Weber substation is 'already serving at its maximum capacity' (equip_aging). Additionally, 'significant distribution load interconnections have been requested in this area' (load_growth). Solution loops French Camp into Bellota-Tesla #2 230 kV line to create a new, stronger 230 kV supply source, bypassing the saturated Weber 60 kV path.
load_growth_evidence: Report states: 'Significant distribution load interconnections have been requested in this area.' Weber substation is at maximum capacity, and new load requests are driving the need for a fundamentally new supply path.

project_name: Eldorado 230 kV Short Circuit Duty Mitigation
brief_description: Split the Eldorado joint-owned 230 kV bus with bus sectionalizing circuit breakers to mitigate short circuit duty (SCD) issues. Scope will include extending the bus and relocating 230 kV lines and other equipment within the substation.
objectives: Reduce the SCD at Eldorado joint-owned 230 kV bus by about 21.4 kA to about 53.9 kA well below the 63 kA breaker rating while retaining operational flexibility and improving safety due to the reduced incident energy
driver_detail: SCD at the joint-owned Eldorado 230 kV bus is expected to exceed 63 kA breaker ratings by 2024. The report explicitly states: 'The increased short circuit levels are due to the addition of renewable generation in the area, along with associated transmission upgrades, interconnecting to NV Energy, Los Angeles Water and Power, and ISO controlled SCE facilities.' Project splits the joint-owned bus with sectionalizing breakers to reduce SCD by ~21.4 kA. Expedited ISO management approval obtained in July 2023 due to urgency.
